description: A single table rendered as an image (no plots or micrographs). The caption reads "Performance comparison of MatSAM and other methods on in-house and public and multiphase datasets", and the table header is Dataset | Metric | Method, with five method columns: MatSAM, SAM, OTSU, Adaptive and Specialist method. Six dataset row-blocks are tabulated: DP590-1, DP590-2, NBS-1 [16], NBS-2 [16], AZA [25] and UHCS [11]. Each block reports the three metrics IoU, F1 and Recall as means with bracketed percentage relative deviations, e.g. DP590-1 IoU 0.77 (±8.2 %). The "Specialist method" column is populated only in the IoU rows (NBS-1 0.77, NBS-2 0.79, AZA 0.97, UHCS 0.71); all other cells are "-" except UHCS Recall 0.88. MatSAM records the best IoU on DP590-1 (0.77), DP590-2 (0.82), NBS-1 (0.91), NBS-2 (0.82) and UHCS (0.76), while on AZA MatSAM 0.96 (±0.6 %) is narrowly below the specialist method 0.97. The Adaptive threshold is weakest on the DP590 datasets (IoU 0.48 and 0.28). OTSU gives the highest Recall on DP590-1 (0.91) and AZA (0.97) but lower IoU. Taken together the table shows the training-free MatSAM delivers the most consistently strong, low-variance segmentation across datasets spanning in-house, public and multiphase types.

observations.observation: The figure is a single rendered data table with header cells 'Dataset', 'Metric' and 'Method', the latter spanning five method columns: MatSAM, SAM, OTSU, Adaptive and Specialist method.
Six datasets appear as row-blocks: DP590-1, DP590-2, NBS-1 [16], NBS-2 [16], AZA [25] and UHCS [11], each reporting IoU, F1 and Recall as mean values with bracketed percentage relative deviations.
MatSAM has the best IoU on five of the six datasets: 0.77 (±8.2 %) DP590-1, 0.82 (±3.1 %) DP590-2, 0.91 (±1.2 %) NBS-1, 0.82 (±6.3 %) NBS-2 and 0.76 (±0.7 %) UHCS.
On the AZA [25] dataset the Specialist method reaches IoU 0.97, marginally above MatSAM's 0.96 (±0.6 %), which is therefore the second-best value there.
The Adaptive method is the weakest on the DP590 datasets, with IoU 0.48 (±5.3 %) and F1 0.49 (±8.9 %) for DP590-1 and IoU 0.28 (±0.9 %) and F1 0.17 (±2.1 %) for DP590-2.
OTSU attains the highest Recall in several blocks (DP590-1 0.91 (±8.6 %), AZA 0.97 (±0.1 %)) despite lower IoU than MatSAM in those blocks.
On UHCS [11] the Adaptive method has a higher Recall (0.93 ±1.3 %) than MatSAM (0.78 ±2.7 %), yet MatSAM's IoU (0.76) is much higher than Adaptive's (0.46).

The 'Specialist method' column is populated only in the IoU rows (NBS-1 0.77, NBS-2 0.79, AZA 0.97, UHCS 0.71) and in the UHCS Recall row (0.88); the DP590-1 and DP590-2 rows show '/' and the remaining cells show '-'.
The largest spread reported is SAM's Recall on DP590-1, 0.66 (±26.0 %); MatSAM's deviations on the public datasets are small, e.g. ±1.2 % (NBS-1 IoU), ±0.6 % (AZA IoU) and ±0.7 % (UHCS IoU).
The caption states that for the primary metric (IoU) bold and underlined values indicate the best and second-best results respectively; the table body carries corresponding emphasis on IoU cells.
The caption states the benchmark covers in-house, public and multiphase datasets, but the table itself contains no column or label identifying which dataset belongs to which category.
All metrics are unitless scores between 0 and 1; the bracketed values are relative deviations expressed in percent, not absolute metric errors.
